Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum with bilateral paratracheal fullness that is more prominent on the right side, causing deviation of the trachea to the left. This appearance is characteristic of mediastinal lymphadenopathy (e.g., from lymphoma or granulomatous disease), which fits the clinical presentation of retrosternal pain in an 11-year-old, whereas there is no evidence of pleural effusion, lung collapse, or a discrete pulmonary mass.
